newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Kepco launches, China eyed.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Kepco launches, China eyed.

text.p: Yankee bonds once again played a major role in Asian debt markets on Wednesday, with South Korea's Kepco launching a bond overnight and China's State Development Bank expected in New York today.
Korea Electric Power Corp launched a US$300 million bond due 2027 via lead manager Goldman Sachs.
The bond, which can be put after 10 years, pays a coupon of seven percent and was priced at par to yield 45 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
Kepco is rated equally with the sovereign at A1 by Moody's Investors Service and AA-minus by Standard and Poor's Corp.
The spread was on the tighter side of expectations.
"The pricing was on the aggressive side, especially given some of the recent softening of spreads for Korean credits," said one syndicate manager.
Bankers said Korea Long-Term Credit Bank is planning a US$200 million floating rate note issue, but the deal won't be mandated for a while.
State Development Bank of China is expected to launch its long-awaited Yankee bond via lead managers J.P. Morgan and Lehman Brothers later today.
Bankers in Asia said they expect the 10-year US$300 million issue to attract substantial demand.
